To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of two bacterial strains (B. cereus S7 & P. alvei T28) significantly suppressed guava wilt disease in two independent glasshouse trials.

(i) the combination of the rhizobacterial isolates Bacillus cereus and Paenibacula lvei suppressed guava wilt disease, and (ii) the plant resistance activator Actigard® (acibenzolar-S-methyl) did not control guava wilt disease.
the combination of the rhizobacterial strain Bacillus cereus strain S7 and Paebibacillus alvai strain T29 is the most effective treatment to suppress guava wilt disease.
